# “Kriya Yoga Meditation for a Happy and Successful Life”

*A World Meditation Day Discourse by a YSS Sannyasi*

### Opening Prayer and Invocation

*"O Cosmic Spirit, Heavenly Father, Mother, Friend, Beloved God! Jesus Christ, Bhagavan Krishna, Mahavatar Babaji, Lahiri Mahasaya, Swami Sri Yukteswar, and our beloved Gurudeva, Paramahansa Yogananda—saints and sages of all religions, we bow to you all.* 

*O Divine Mother, charge our minds with Thy light, charge our hearts with Thy love, and charge our souls with Thy joy. Lift us from the consciousness of body-limitations into the omnipresent realm of Thy peace. May Thy love shine forever on the sanctuary of our devotion, and may we be able to awaken Thy love in all hearts. Om. Shanti. Shanti. Shanti."*

---

## Introduction: The Universal Search for Joy

Jai Guru, dear souls. I welcome you all on this auspicious occasion of World Meditation Day. It is a joy to behold so many seekers, gathered not just in physical space but in spiritual attunement, united in the singular quest that defines all human existence: the search for lasting happiness and true success.

Every human being, from the moment of their first breath to the moment of their transition from this world, is engaged in a tireless search. If you ask a businessman why he works so hard, he will say it is to make his business successful. If you ask why he wants success, he will say it is to provide comfort and happiness for his family. If you ask a student why they study, a mother why she cares for her child, or an artist why they paint—at the root of every single human action is the desire to attain joy and to avoid suffering. 

Yet, as we look around the world today, we see a paradox. We live in an age of unprecedented material comfort, technological advancement, and endless avenues of entertainment. And yet, humanity is plagued by anxiety, stress, loneliness, and a deep, gnawing sense of emptiness. Why is this so? 

Our beloved Gurudeva, Paramahansa Yogananda, gave us the answer in his timeless teachings. He said that we are searching for the right thing in the wrong place. We are searching for an infinite, unconditioned joy in finite, conditioned worldly objects. Worldly happiness is like a mirage in a desert—it promises water but yields only dry sand. True, lasting, unshakeable happiness—which our scriptures call *Ananda* (Divine Bliss)—cannot be found outside of ourselves. It can only be found in the quiet sanctuary of our own souls, through the practice of scientific meditation.

Today, we will explore how the ancient, sacred science of **Kriya Yoga** acts as the ultimate key to unlocking a life of absolute happiness and supreme success.

---

## Section 1: Redefining Happiness and Success

Before we can achieve happiness and success, we must first understand what they truly mean. 

Most people define happiness as a state of mind that depends on external circumstances. They say, "If I get that job, if I buy that house, if people treat me well, then I will be happy." But this is conditional happiness. It is a hostage to fortune. The moment circumstances change—and change they will, for change is the very nature of this dualistic universe—that happiness vanishes.

True happiness is **Joy**. Gurudeva defined Joy as *"a state of mind that does not depend on any external condition; it is self-born, ever-new, and completely independent of what is happening around you."* It is the very nature of your soul. You do not have to *acquire* happiness; you only have to *remember* who you are.

Similarly, what is true success? Is it merely the accumulation of wealth, power, and prestige? No. How many millionaires suffer from insomnia and ulcers? How many famous personalities are driven to despair? Gurudeva gave a magnificent, revolutionary definition of success: 

> *"Success is the ability to create, at will, what you need when you need it; and it is the realization of your oneness with the Divine Source of all power, wisdom, and abundance."*

True success means that you are the master of your mind, not its slave. It means that you can face the battles of life with an unshakeable smile, knowing that your inner wealth can never be stolen by any external circumstance. Kriya Yoga is the practical method to achieve this supreme state of inner mastery.

**Story • The Wave That Forgot It Was the Ocean**

Story: There was once a small wave rippling across the vast surface of the Pacific Ocean. As it rode high on the wind, it looked at the other waves around it and felt a sense of pride. "Look at how high I am, look at how beautiful my crest is!" But as the wind began to die down and it approached the shallow shores, the wave saw other waves crashing against the jagged rocks and dissolving into nothingness. It became terrified of its impending end, crying out in fear, "I am going to die! I am going to be destroyed! My existence is coming to a painful end!"

Another wave, larger, wiser, and much deeper, saw its distress and smiled. "Why are you crying, my friend?" the larger wave asked.

"Can't you see?" the small wave sobbed, "We are going to crash and disappear! This is the end of my life!"

The wise wave replied softly, "Do not fear, my child. You are looking only at your outward form. You think you are just a temporary wave, but that is merely a passing shape. In reality, you are the water. You are the vast, immortal ocean. When the wave-form disappears, you do not die—you simply merge back into the ocean from which you came. Realize your true nature as water, and all your fear will vanish."

---

## Section 2: Kriya Yoga—The Royal Highway to the Soul

This beautiful parable represents our current human plight. We have forgotten that we are the vast ocean of Spirit, and we have mistakenly identified ourselves with the tiny, fragile wave of the physical body and ego. Kriya Yoga is the scientific technique that dissolves this delusion and reminds us of our oceanic nature.

What is Kriya Yoga? It is not a system of dogmatic beliefs, nor is it a set of simple physical postures. Kriya is an advanced, psychophysiological technique of pranayama (life-force control) that was revived for this modern age by Mahavatar Babaji, handed down to Lahiri Mahasaya, Swami Sri Yukteswar, and brought to the West and the world by our Guru, Paramahansa Yogananda.

To understand how Kriya works, we must look at the relationship between the breath, the mind, and the spine. 

When your mind is restless, angry, or anxious, your breath is fast and shallow. When you are calm, deep in thought, or about to fall asleep, your breath naturally slows down. This is a scientific fact: **there is a direct, mathematical relationship between the rate of your breath and the state of your mind.**

As long as the life-force (Prana) is constantly flowing outward through the five senses—sight, hearing, smell, taste, and touch—the mind is bombarded with external sensations. It is like trying to see your reflection in a lake that is constantly being whipped by strong winds; the ripples make it impossible to see clearly. 

By practicing Kriya Yoga, the yogi directs the life-force up and down the spiritual highway of the spine—the *Sushumna*. This process carbonizes the venous blood and recharges it with pure oxygen, decelerating the heart and calming the nervous system. As the heart slows down and the breath becomes naturally quiet, the life-force is withdrawn from the five senses and directed inward toward the higher brain centers, specifically the spiritual eye (*Kutastha Chaitanya*) at the point between the eyebrows.

In this state of quietude, the storm of sensory perceptions ceases. The restless ripples on the lake of the mind subside, and in that perfectly still water, you see your true reflection: not a mortal, struggling physical body, but the immortal, blissful soul.

**Story • Lahiri Mahasaya and the Restless Clerk**

Story: A busy railway clerk once came to the great master Lahiri Mahasaya in Varanasi. The clerk was highly stressed, burdened by his worldly duties, a demanding job, a large family, and endless financial worries. He fell at the master's feet and lamented, "Yogiraj, how can a poor, busy householder like me ever find peace or God? I have no time to sit in a cave and meditate for hours. My mind is constantly filled with anxieties. Spiritual life seems to be only for those who have renounced the world."

Lahiri Mahasaya looked at him with eyes full of infinite compassion and said, "My son, God is not found only in caves. He is in your heart. You do not need to give up your duties; you only need to change your focus. You must learn to perform your actions with the Lord in your heart."

The Master then initiated him into the sacred art of Kriya Yoga, teaching him how to perceive the silent current of peace in the spine even while performing his clerical duties. By practicing just a few minutes of Kriya before work and after coming home, the clerk soon transformed. He found that his concentration and efficiency increased dramatically. His short temper vanished, and his mind remained anchored in a state of unshakeable joy even amidst the clatter and chaos of the railway station. He realized that Kriya Yoga is the ultimate practical path for the modern householder.

---

## Section 3: The Path to Absolute Happiness

How does Kriya Yoga lead us to a happy life? 

First, it frees us from the tyranny of our moods. Most people's happiness is dictated by their morning mood. If they wake up feeling grumpy, their entire day is ruined. But a Kriya Yogi, through daily practice, accesses a reservoir of joy that is independent of physical conditions. By calming the nervous system, Kriya neutralizes the *vrittis*—the whirlpools of feeling and emotion in the heart. 

When you sit in deep meditation and feel that cool, divine current rising up your spine, a profound peace begins to steal over your consciousness. You feel a joy so sweet, so deep, that all the pleasures of the world pale in comparison. When you rise from your meditation seat, that joy stays with you. It becomes a "portable heaven" that you carry with you wherever you go.

Secondly, Kriya Yoga gives us the power of resilience. Life will always bring challenges—financial difficulties, health issues, the loss of loved ones, and social conflicts. But the yogi who meditates daily has an anchor. When the storms of life hit, they are not swept away. They are like a deep-rooted oak tree that stands firm because its roots are sunk deep into the soil of divine consciousness.

**Story • The Quest of the Musk Deer**

Story: In the high, pristine regions of the Himalayas lives the Musk Deer, known as the *Kasturi Mriga*. This deer carries a sack of highly fragrant musk deep within its own navel. As the wind blows through the mountains, the exquisite, intoxicating scent of this musk is carried to the deer's nostrils.

Entranced by the beautiful aroma, the deer looks around, wondering, "Where is this magnificent fragrance coming from?" Believing it to be somewhere outside itself, the deer begins a frantic search. It runs wild through the thorny bushes, leaps across deep crevices, climbs steep, dangerous cliffs, and exhausts its life force searching everywhere in the external world. In its desperate chase, it often falls from a cliff or collapses from sheer exhaustion, never realizing that the source of the fragrance it was searching for was inside its own body all along.

In the same way, we are like that musk deer. The fragrance of love, peace, and joy is within our own souls, yet we run frantically in the external forest of the world, exhausting ourselves, only to find disappointment. Kriya Yoga teaches us to stop the outward search and look within.

---

## Section 4: Kriya Yoga for a Successful and Dynamic Life

There is a common misconception that meditation makes a person passive, aloof, or impractical. Some believe that to seek God, one must abandon all ambition and withdraw from active life. 

Nothing could be further from the truth! Kriya Yoga is the path of dynamic action. Paramahansa Yogananda was a magnificent example of this. He built a global organization, wrote spiritual classics, traveled the world, and managed complex affairs, yet his mind was always anchored in God. 

Kriya Yoga enhances your outer success in several profound ways:

1. **Unparalleled Focus and Concentration**: The average human mind is highly fragmented. We are thinking about ten things at once, which dilutes our mental power. Kriya Yoga calms the brain cells and sharpens the concentration. When you focus your entire mind on a single task, success is inevitable.
2. **Awakening of Intuition**: The logical mind has limitations; it can only work with the data provided by the senses. But the soul has the power of *intuition*—direct soul-perception. Through deep Kriya meditation, you tap into this superconscious intuition. You will find yourself making the right decisions, choosing the right paths, and solving complex problems effortlessly because you are guided by the whisper of the Divine within.
3. **Vitality and Magnetic Energy**: By drawing cosmic energy into the body through the medulla oblongata, Kriya recharges the physical form with life-force. You feel dynamic, enthusiastic, and untiring. This inner vitality creates a positive magnetism that attracts success, opportunities, and the right people into your life.

---

## Section 5: The Sacred Commitment of Sadhana

Dear friends, to experience these benefits, consistency is key. Meditation is not a hobby to be practiced only when we feel like it. It is a daily spiritual necessity—our *Sadhana*.

Make a sacred commitment to yourself and to Gurudeva on this World Meditation Day. Dedicate a portion of your morning and evening to silence. Even if it is just fifteen minutes or half an hour, establish a daily routine. Put aside your phones, your worries, and your to-do lists, and sit quietly in the presence of the Divine.

Begin with the YSS/SRF Energization Exercises to prepare the body, practice the Hong-Sau technique of concentration, and if you are initiated, practice your Kriya Yoga with deep love and devotion. Remember, Kriya is not a mechanical exercise; it is a love offering of your life-force to the Divine.

As you practice regularly, you will find a subtle transformation taking place. You will find yourself becoming kinder, calmer, and more loving. The things that used to irritate you will no longer have power over you. You will find that you are more successful in your daily duties, and most importantly, you will feel a sweet, constant companionship with God.

---

### Conclusion and Blessing

Let us close our eyes for a moment, sit erect, and draw our attention to the point between the eyebrows—the seat of the spiritual eye.

Feel the great lineage of our Gurus blessing you today. They are not historical figures of the past; they are living, loving presences, ready to guide you back to your divine home. 

May you walk this path of Kriya Yoga with determination, courage, and joy. May you realize that you are not a limited mortal wave, but the immortal, blissful ocean of Spirit. May your life be crowned with true success, and may your heart overflow with the ever-new joy of God.

*"O Divine Mother, may Thy love shine forever on the sanctuary of our devotion, and may we be able to awaken Thy love in all hearts."*

**Jai Guru. Om. Shanti. Shanti. Shanti.**
